stories.headline: Friday Pressers
stories.deck: Luka Vušković fit again for Brighton, with Hadjam back and Dunk a rotation doubt
stories.body:
Fabian Hurzeler declared Luka Vušković fit again and back in contention, Brighton's clearest gain before the deadline. He stopped short of naming a line-up, and left Lewis Dunk's involvement open with rotation on the table.

Jaouen Hadjam returns alongside Vušković, so Hurzeler has options restored at the back that he did not have a week ago.

teamNews.line: Unai Emery ruled out Marco Bizot and left a question mark over Joao Gomes.
Harry Wilson goes into the weekend under a cloud.
Nothing new from Crystal Palace ahead of the deadline.
Kenny Tete will not feature for Fulham.
Nothing new from Ipswich Town.
No fresh word from Liverpool.
Manchester United added nothing to a settled list.
Nothing new from Sunderland.
David Moyes ruled Merlin Röhl out without detailing the reason.
Roberto De Zerbi left Pedro Porro's involvement in doubt.
Mikel Arteta welcomed two men back into contention.
Fabian Hurzeler had two fit again and stopped short of committing to Lewis Dunk.

stories.headline: Thursday Pressers
stories.deck: João Pedro a Chelsea doubt for the deadline, no complaint given
stories.body:
João Pedro sits as a doubt for Chelsea, with Xabi Alonso stopping short of clearing him and giving no update on what keeps him on the edge of it.

Whether test211's man features is a decision left open, and nothing said points to a timescale.

teamNews.line: Xabi Alonso would not commit either way on João Pedro before the deadline.
Matthias Jaissle flagged Amar Dedic as a fitness question.
Sergej Jakirovic left Matt Targett uncertain for the weekend.
Frank Lampard ruled Aurèle Amenda out entirely.
Nothing new came out of Nottingham Forest.
Brentford added nothing to their list.

stories.headline: Lawro's Predictions: GW6
stories.deck: Lawro goes against the favourites in test3 v test2, and leaves test4 v 123 to the front-runners.
stories.body: First column here, and no record to answer for yet. That comes soon enough. Twenty-two years of Saturday scores on the BBC, and now this. Preston weather, then.

ties.line: test3 are the favourites, and I fancy test2 anyway. Why? Isak. He is up against Manchester City, a tough defence, and none of that bothers a Liverpool man one bit. Gonzalo of Fulham has gone quiet for test3, no goal and no assist in his last two. Havertz of Arsenal has done the same for test2, so that pair cancel out. Both lost last week. Sitting through this one will feel like waiting for a bus that never turns up. I'll go with test2.

123 top the table and look the part. Haaland of Manchester City has scored in each of his last two. Good news? Not for test4. Mbeumo of Manchester United has gone dry for test4, no goal and no assist in two. Fernandes of Manchester United, same story for 123, so it's not all one way. Foden is suspended for test4, and that's that. Both sides came off a win last week. I'd be surprised if the front-runners slipped here. 123 for me.

stories.headline: Gross profit for 123 at the front
stories.deck: 123 lead test2 26-16

matchups.standfirst: Brighton midfielder Pascal Gross gave 123 a goal and an assist on Saturday.
paragraphs: Saturday brought returns at both ends. Newcastle defender Lewis Hall scored for test2, eight points in all. Gross added his goal and his assist for 123, and the gap came down from 11 to 10.

Millar did not play for test2, so Sunderland defender Thomas Meunier comes on if he plays, away to Man City on Sunday. James Trafford is at home to Crystal Palace, and Trai Hume travels for 123. test2 have four still to play, 123 five.

matchups.standfirst: test3 built the lead in two stages, first in the day's play and then off the bench.
paragraphs: test3 scored 15 to test4's five, with Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford keeping a shut-out for seven points. That made it 15-5.

The reserves widened it. Ipswich Town defender Leif Davis returned two points for test4, in for a man who did not play. Luka Vuskovic kept a clean sheet for test3, nine points to two that pushed the gap from 10 to 17.
James Justin is at home to Crystal Palace for test4, and Harry Maguire goes to Fulham for test3. test4 have seven men left and test3 three.

stories.headline: test3 beat test4 33-28
stories.deck: 123 beat test2 38-37

matchups.standfirst: 123 edged it by a single point, and one goal from Erling Haaland made all the difference.
paragraphs: Friday gave 123 an early cushion at 11-0. test2 answered on Saturday, Newcastle defender Lewis Hall scoring for eight to begin the chase, though Pascal Gross replied with a goal and an assist for an 11-point haul, and the margin held at 26-16.

Sunday brought the fightback properly alive. James Trafford kept a shut-out, Alexander Isak scored, and Matheus Cunha added another in the 89th minute. Haaland answered for 123 in the 81st, his six points holding the gap at four, 38-34. Thomas Meunier then laid one on among the substitutions to close it to 38-37.

test2 won three of the four stages and still lost. Reinildo did not play for 123, available again now his one-match suspension is served. test2 fell to third and 123 rose to second. test2 play test3 next, 123 face test4.

stories.headline: Brobbey's treble no robbery
stories.deck: Manchester City beat Sunderland 5-3

reports.standfirst: Manchester City beat Sunderland 5-3 to stay top with a fifth win running, Brian Brobbey's hat-trick counting for nothing.
reports.account:
Brian Brobbey scored three times for Sunderland and finished on the losing side.
Nilson Angulo shot wide from inside the box after Enzo Le Fée crossed, in the 6th minute.
Enzo Fernández put Manchester City ahead after nine minutes, and Brobbey answered three minutes later, taking a through ball from Le Fée.
Erling Haaland shot off target from inside the six-yard box after Iliman Ndiaye's cross.
Rayan Cherki restored the City lead in the 29th minute from an Antoine Semenyo pass, before Brobbey levelled again, Thomas Meunier supplying him after 33 minutes.
Semenyo made it 3-2 just before half-time, finishing a Marc Guéhi pass from a corner.
Semenyo struck again after 57 minutes, and Brobbey completed his hat-trick two minutes later, set up by Angulo from a set piece.
Rúben Dias headed a Fernández corner off target midway through the second half.
Haaland settled it with nine minutes left, taking a pass from Josko Gvardiol for 5-3.

sections.head: Semenyo among the goals
sections.pitch: Semenyo made three chances across the match and set up the third City goal.
sections.stake: He is test1's man and returned 13 points.

sections.head: Haaland strikes late
sections.pitch: Haaland had four shots in all, one of them the goal that ended the scoring.
sections.stake: He belongs to 123 for six points, and 123 lead test2 38-34 in their head-to-head this period.

sections.head: Gvardiol makes fifth
sections.pitch: Gvardiol laid on the fifth for Haaland.
sections.stake: He was on test31121's bench, so those points did not count.

reports.standfirst: Liverpool won 1-0 at AFC Bournemouth through Alexander Isak, extending their unbeaten start to five and leaving the hosts still chasing a first win.
reports.account:
Evanilson was denied from six yards after 18 minutes, Marcus Tavernier the maker with a cross.
Bradley Barcola forced a save after 33 minutes, Alexander Isak the supplier.
Ryan Christie dragged wide from close range after 53 minutes, Rayan crossing.
Isak settled it after 57 minutes, Liverpool's only goal from three efforts on target.
AFC Bournemouth carved out one clear opening and did not take it.

sections.head: Wirtz withdrawn
sections.pitch: Wirtz made three chances before he was taken off.
sections.stake: He belongs to test1, for whom he scored six points.

sections.head: Christie starts
sections.pitch: Christie made his first league start of the season, had four shots and was then taken off.
sections.stake: He is a free agent.

reports.standfirst: Leeds United and Crystal Palace drew 0-0, Palace keeping their first clean sheet of the season.
reports.account:
Tarik Muharemovic headed a corner off target after eight minutes, Anton Stach crossing.
Jefferson Lerma shot off target from close range from a corner early in the second half.
Tyrick Mitchell had the ball in the net after 52 minutes, only for a video review to rule it out.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin had openings for Leeds and did not take them.
Daichi Kamada headed wide from inside the six-yard box with five minutes left.

sections.head: Trafford keeps it clean
sections.pitch: Trafford made five saves for his clean sheet.
sections.stake: He is test2's keeper for seven points, though 123 lead test2 38-34 in their head-to-head this period.

sections.head: Muharemovic shoots often
sections.pitch: Muharemovic had four shots across the match.
sections.stake: He was on test211's bench.

reports.standfirst: Fulham drew 1-1 with Manchester United, conceding one minute from time to stay in the bottom three and without a win this season.
reports.account:
Gonzalo García shot off target after four minutes, Antonee Robinson the maker.
Bryan Mbeumo headed wide after 11 minutes, Marcus Rashford crossing from a corner.
Bruno Fernandes struck the woodwork after 25 minutes.
Lisandro Martínez turned into his own net after 63 minutes to put Fulham ahead.
Patrick Dorgu came on with six minutes left and had a hand in the leveller.
One minute from time Matheus Cunha drew United level, taking Dorgu's pass and striking it right-footed from outside the box, low into the corner.
Dorgu then headed over from six yards in stoppage time, Mbeumo delivering the cross.
Fulham managed a single goal from six efforts on target and made three clear chances without a return.

sections.head: Cunha finds the corner
sections.pitch: Cunha had three shots and created three chances besides his goal.
sections.stake: He is test2's, and six points spares them a blank.

sections.head: Iwobi creates plenty
sections.pitch: Iwobi made five chances for Fulham before he was taken off.
sections.stake: A free agent.

stories.headline: Spurs left with van Hecke of a comeback
stories.deck: Aston Villa won 3-2 at Tottenham Hotspur

reports.standfirst: Aston Villa won 3-2 at Tottenham for their first win of the season, lifting Emery's side clear of the bottom three, where without a win Spurs remain.
reports.account:
Aston Villa were 3-0 up with 11 minutes left, and Tottenham then scored twice from the 80th minute.
Sávio drew a save with a shot inside the box, set up by Dominic Solanke, in the 11th minute.
Johan Manzambi tested the keeper four minutes later, Victor Lindelöf the provider.
Pedro Porro went off injured in the 19th minute.
Emiliano Buendía saw a shot saved in the 27th minute, Nicolas Jackson supplying him.
Manzambi struck just before the interval, Boubacar Kamara the passer, for 1-0.
Mohammed Kudus came on at half-time.
Kudus had the ball in the net on the hour, made by Solanke, but a video review ruled it out.
Jackson made it 2-0 midway through the second half, Manzambi turning provider on this one.
Buendía added the third with 11 minutes left, John McGinn feeding him from a break down the flank, and he struck it right-footed from outside the box into the top corner.
Conor Gallagher came on with six minutes remaining.
Gallagher pulled one back four minutes from time, Kudus the maker.
Jan Paul van Hecke headed home Andy Robertson's set-piece cross deep into stoppage time for 3-2.

sections.head: Buendía finds range
sections.pitch: Buendía had three efforts across the match and created three chances for others besides his goal.
sections.stake: Notemail has him, worth seven points that day.

sections.head: Manzambi makes mark
sections.pitch: Manzambi took his first league start of the campaign and was withdrawn, having had four attempts and laid on Jackson's second.
sections.stake: He belongs to nobody in the league and has one league goal this season.

sections.head: Sávio busy, unrewarded
sections.pitch: Sávio had three shots and set up four openings for team-mates across the match.
sections.stake: He is going unclaimed in the league.

reports.standfirst: Brighton beat Arsenal 3-0 to push them off top place and hand them a first defeat of the season.
reports.account:
Pascal Groß opened the scoring after 31 minutes. Charalampos Kostoulas laid it back and Groß struck it right-footed from outside the box into the middle of the goal.
Kostoulas doubled it on half-time, finishing a Diego Gómez pass on the break.
Chema Andrés headed in a Groß corner after 57 minutes to make it 3-0.
Pascal Struijk met a De Cuyper corner with a header from close range after 68 minutes, off target.
Riccardo Calafiori then nodded a Declan Rice corner wide from inside the six-yard box, and Kai Havertz headed a Bukayo Saka corner off target too.
Struijk went off injured four minutes from time.
Malick Yalcouyé struck the woodwork after 90 minutes.

sections.head: Groß runs it
sections.pitch: Pascal Groß has three league goals this season and crossed the corner that Chema Andrés headed in.
sections.stake: 123 have him for 11 points, and in their head-to-head this period 123 lead test2 38-34.

sections.head: Kostoulas among the goals
sections.pitch: Charalampos Kostoulas has two league goals this season, had four shots and set up the second before he was taken off.
sections.stake: test31121 have him for eight points.

reports.standfirst: Everton beat 10-man Ipswich 1-0, a fifth match unbeaten for Moyes's side.
reports.account:
Brennan Johnson pulled an early chance off target in the 5th minute, Harrison Armstrong threading him through from inside the box.
Thierno Barry put Everton ahead in the 11th minute, James Tarkowski the provider.
Leif Davis shot over from the six-yard box in the 38th minute, Abdul Fatawu crossing.
Barry had the ball in the net again after 58 minutes, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall the maker, but a video review ruled it out.
Abdul Fatawu was sent off for a second booking midway through the second half.
Dewsbury-Hall put a header wide from the six-yard box with 14 minutes left, Tyler Dibling the crosser.
Emersonn went off injured with nine minutes left.

sections.head: Barry strikes early
sections.pitch: Barry had three efforts across the match and now stands on two league goals this season.
sections.stake: Notemail has him, worth six points.

sections.head: Pickford keeps clean sheet
sections.pitch: Pickford made four saves to keep his goal intact.
sections.stake: test3 has him, at seven points; in the head-to-head this period test4 lead test3 26-24.

reports.standfirst: Newcastle held off Hull 2-1 for a first home win of the season, ending Hull's unbeaten start.
reports.account:
Joe Willock struck after three minutes, converting a Harvey Barnes pass.
Lewis Hall made it 2-0 four minutes later on the break, again teed up by Barnes.
Hall shot off target from the six-yard box after 33 minutes, Jacob Murphy crossing.
Yoane Wissa saw a penalty saved just before the interval.
Sven Botman was denied a header from a Hall cross after 52 minutes.
Mohamed Belloumi shot off target on the break at the other end.
Mohamed-Ali Cho came on midway through the half and pulled one back a minute on. Belloumi threaded him through and he finished left-footed from inside the box, low into the corner.
Sean Steur and then Matias Fernandez-Pardo both went off injured.

sections.head: Barnes turns creator
sections.pitch: Harvey Barnes made both Newcastle goals and three chances in all.
sections.stake: testf has him for eight points.

sections.head: Belloumi busy in defeat
sections.pitch: Mohamed Belloumi had five shots and set up Cho's goal before being taken off.
sections.stake: Notemail has him for four points.

reports.standfirst: Coventry won 1-0 at Nottingham Forest for a first win and first clean sheet of the season, though still in the bottom three.
reports.account:
Dan Ndoye shot off target inside the box after 13 minutes, Neco Williams nodding it to him.
Brandon Thomas-Asante headed a Jay Dasilva cross off target after 28 minutes.
Murillo headed a Williams corner off target from the six-yard box.
Dasilva settled it after 55 minutes. Carl Rushworth found him and he finished left-footed from inside the box into the middle of the goal.
Igor Jesus seemed to have levelled four minutes from time, but a video review ruled it out.

sections.head: Rushworth turns provider
sections.pitch: Carl Rushworth set up Dasilva's winner and kept a clean sheet at the back.
sections.stake: test211 has him on the bench, so his points did not count.

sections.head: Gibbs-White carves without reward
sections.pitch: Morgan Gibbs-White made six chances, none of them converted.
sections.stake: test3 has him.

stories.headline: Chelsea left holding the ball
stories.deck: Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0

reports.standfirst: Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0, three second-half goals lifting Keith Andrews's unbeaten side above the visitors and into third.
reports.account:
Igor Thiago had the first sight of goal after five minutes, meeting a Yehor Yarmoliuk cross with a shot that flew off target.
Pedro Neto replied for Chelsea after 10 minutes, working a chance from a Danny Welbeck pass, but Caoimhín Kelleher saved.
Just before half-time Keane Lewis-Potter was set up by Jaidon Anthony, only for his shot to be turned away.
The opening goal came after 61 minutes. Jannik Schuster headed a corner across goal and Jaidon Anthony finished for 1-0.
With seven minutes left Thiago made it 2-0 on the break, Brentford's second in the space of 11 minutes.
Fábio Carvalho came on three minutes from time.
Four minutes into added time Carvalho added the third. From within the six-yard box he swept a right-footed finish into the top corner for 3-0.

sections.head: Schade threatens
sections.pitch: Kevin Schade had three shots without a goal.
sections.stake: 123 has him for eight points, and 123 lead their head-to-head 38-34 this period.

sections.head: Schuster provides
sections.pitch: Jannik Schuster made the opening goal with his header from the corner.
sections.stake: He is a free agent.

sections.head: Thiago among the goals
sections.pitch: Igor Thiago had three shots across the match, one of them a goal.
sections.stake: He too is a free agent.

stories.headline: Predicted Line-Ups: Gameweek 6
stories.deck: Every club's expected starting eleven for the round, match by match.
stories.body: All 10 of the round's matches, with both sides named.

stories.headline: Predicted Line-Ups: Gameweek 7
stories.deck: Every club's expected starting eleven for the gameweek.

stories.headline: Friday Pressers
stories.deck: Branthwaite a doubt for Everton with a dead leg
stories.body: Jarrad Branthwaite is a doubt for Everton with a dead leg. The problem came early in their last match and has been assessed through the week.

men.name: Jarrad Branthwaite
men.note: dead leg; assessed through the week

quote.text: Jarrad [Branthwaite] had a little problem really early in the game, so we’ve been having a look at that in the week a little bit.

teamNews.line: Phil Foden is available after the international break and his red card, and rest is being considered for Enzo among the most heavily used players.

men.name: Phil Foden
men.note: back after the red card against United; training well

men.name: Enzo
men.note: rest under consideration after heavy minutes

quote.text: During the international break and since the red card against United has been quite long, but he’s training well, doing well since we started, very positive, very good.

teamNews.line: Nicolò Savona is ruled out with a knee injury and Igor Jesus with a calf problem, while Morgan Gibbs-White could rejoin training on Saturday.

quote.text: Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt. He couldn’t train the entire week with us. It looks like he can join tomorrow’s session.

teamNews.line: Two players returning from different injuries have trained on the grass, with their workload to be judged on Saturday.

quote.text: Jannik and Kev have been on the grass this week and we’ll see what tomorrow brings in terms of how much they can do.

teamNews.line: Mikel Merino returns to contention.

quote.text: Piero is evolving really well. Knowing his character and the way he pushes, I’m sure it’s not going to take long. But he will need probably another week or two.

teamNews.line: Reece James is out for several weeks, with no return expected before Christmas.

quote.text: We don’t set timelines but he will be out for several weeks. It won’t be short. We will see after Christmas, time will tell.

teamNews.line: Pascal Stuijk is given another day of recovery, with a decision on him due on Saturday.

quote.text: With Yankuba Minteh and Mats Wieffer we could see quite a quick return.

teamNews.line: Ross Barkley is a doubt.
Joe Rodon misses gameweek 7 but is edging closer to team training.

quote.text: Joe will still miss this game on week seven so edging closer, good progress. Won’t be too long until team training but not yet.

teamNews.line: Hugo Larsson's groin was being checked on Friday ahead of Saturday, and Antonee Robinson is ruled out.

quote.text: We have a small problem with Hugo – his groin. We will check today, but I’m not sure if he will be okay for tomorrow.

teamNews.line: An MRI on Alex Scott came back better than expected, and his rehab can now progress, though he is not ready for Sunderland.

quote.text: We can bring him back on the pitch to start and see how he responds, and we are not talking about six to eight weeks anymore.

teamNews.line: Abdul Fatawu is suspended.

stories.headline: Here we go! Jeremy Doku to Dome
stories.deck: Dome get Jeremy Doku from Truffles for Eberechi Eze
stories.body:
Dome land Jeremy Doku from Truffles, the Manchester City man good for nine points and a goal this season. Truffles take Eberechi Eze the other way, four points and no goals so far for the Arsenal midfielder. Straight swap, both sides moving on a man they drafted elsewhere.

Here we go!

stories.headline: Lawro's Predictions: GW7
stories.deck: Lawro backs two outsiders this week, The Truffle Pigs against Bayern Bru and domeitalycoach against Hazza Maguazza's Redempshazza.
stories.body: Four from five last week, which worries me. One from two on the hunches. Twenty-two years marked in front of the nation, and now a league named after a coffee shop marks me.

ties.line:
GlengarryHearts have Anderson at home to Ipswich Town, who stop nothing that comes at them. Schade of Brentford has two assists for GlengarryHearts from his last two games, and not a goal.

McBurnie goes to Fulham with Hull City for its_ohi, and Fulham frighten nobody. He hasn't scored or set one up lately, and a lamp post moves more. Rayan of AFC Bournemouth is no better for its_ohi.

GlengarryHearts, because a soft opponent beats two quiet men.

Thiago has a goal and an assist for The Truffle Pigs in a fortnight with Brentford. In the Steve Clarke Classic he meets Liverpool, and Jacquet and A.Becker, two more Truffle Pigs men. Fancy owning a man who plays against your own goalkeeper.

Bayern Bru beat GlengarryHearts and now think they're a side. Barcola belongs to Bayern Bru and plays for Liverpool against Thiago. Bayern Bru go in as favourites, and I'm not having it.

The Truffle Pigs, because Jacquet defends properly and A.Becker catches everything they hit at him.

I can't make Cowthenbeef out, and the Teachers' Classic won't help. Cherki gets Cowthenbeef a free hit, Ipswich Town at home. Cowthenbeef went to the waiver list for Gudmundsson of Leeds United, and if he were any good he'd have gone weeks ago.

AtleticoTimHortons have Semenyo with two goals and an assist in his last couple for Manchester City. Runs like that end, usually the week I back them.

AtleticoTimHortons, because goals in the boots trump a defender nobody else wanted.

Doubts first, because Arsenal men have gone quiet all over this league. domeitalycoach hold Havertz, with no goal and no assist from two games. Sitting through his matches these days has been a chore. They also hold Wirtz and Szoboszlai, who face Brentford with Liverpool and will enjoy themselves.

Hazza Maguazza's Redempshazza are bottom, and the redemption is taking its time. Saka has gone the same way, no goal and no assist.

Hazza Maguazza's Redempshazza are fancied and I'm not having it, because Wirtz and Szoboszlai are the best footballers here.

Haaland takes The Raccoons into the Big Man Bakar Derby with Ipswich Town at home. Champions waste a gift like that out of habit. Palmer of Chelsea has two assists for The Raccoons in his last pair, without scoring.

If anyone can, Bannan can. Can they? No. If anyone can, Bannan can have Rogers going to Everton with Chelsea and Gibbs-White of Nottingham Forest gone dry.

The Raccoons, since Ipswich Town at home is a gift even champions can't refuse.

stories.headline: Thursday Pressers
stories.deck: Nobel Mendy out for Hull City, Mohamed-Ali Cho a doubt with a calf problem
stories.body: Nobel Mendy does not play for Hull City, Sergej Jakirovic said.

teamNews.line: Ryan Gravenberch is suspended, and the players who were not ready for Wednesday's match have not been ruled out, with Friday's training still to come.

quote.text: Obviously, they were not ready for last night. We have to wait and see. I think it’s still very early but the same way I said they are not available for the previous games, I leave the chance open this time, yes.

teamNews.line: Anthony Elanga is being brought back slowly after many weeks out, with partial training hoped for the following week.

quote.text: Unfortunately, Anthony’s been out for many weeks so now it’s the process to bring him back slowly but surely in a smart way. Hopefully next week he’s about to train again, at least partially, and then we can reintegrate him step by step.

teamNews.line: Sergej Jakirovic rules out Lucas Gourna-Douath and Nobel Mendy, while Mohamed-Ali Cho is a doubt with a calf problem.
Taiwo Awoniyi is suspended, Josh Eccles is not yet training with an ankle problem, and Luke Woolfenden faces a longer absence still.

quote.text: He’s got a little bit of an issue with his ankle – the calf is fine – so he’s not on the training just yet, we hope so in the next 2-3 weeks to progress. And Woolfenden is a little bit longer than that.

stories.headline: Stach stashed safely in the eleven
stories.deck: Cowthenbeef beat The Truffle Pigs 46-44

matchups.standfirst: The goal from Crystal Palace's Daichi Kamada stayed on The Truffle Pigs' bench, while Stach blanked in the eleven for three points.
paragraphs: Kamada's goal helped the Eagles to a 3-1 win against Nott'm Forest. For Cowthenbeef, Chelsea's João Pedro struck twice as the Blues put five past Bournemouth.
Igor Thiago and Johan Manzambi each made an assist when Aston Villa and Brentford drew 2-2, so that match settled nothing between the two sides.
Ferdi Kadıoğlu, in The Truffle Pigs' eleven for the first time, kept a clean sheet for Brighton at Sunderland. Bart Verbruggen kept one in the same match for Cowthenbeef.

matchups.verdict: its_ohi beat If anyone can, Bannan can 40-34
matchups.standfirst: its_ohi signed Aston Villa's John McGinn this gameweek, and he gave them a goal at once.
paragraphs: McGinn struck when Aston Villa and Brentford drew 2-2, and Emiliano Buendía made an assist in the same match for its_ohi.
Chelsea's Morgan Rogers was among the finest men in the Blues' 5-1 win against Bournemouth, and his goal there was the biggest return for If anyone can, Bannan can.
Francisco Evanilson replied for Bournemouth in the 51st minute, and that goal for If anyone can, Bannan can cost Martinez his clean sheet for its_ohi.

matchups.standfirst: AtleticoTimHortons found goals from defence and attack, and Hazza Maguazza's Redempshazza had a single assist to answer them.
paragraphs: Brighton's De Cuyper was the finest man in the Seagulls' 2-0 victory at Sunderland, and one of those goals was his.

Arsenal's Riccardo Calafiori led the way against Leeds, and his goal in the 62nd minute cost Bogle his clean sheet for Hazza Maguazza's Redempshazza. Benjamin White, making his first appearance in their eleven, set up a goal in that 2-1 win for the Gunners.
Dan Ndoye, new to the AtleticoTimHortons eleven, added a goal in Crystal Palace's 3-1 win against Nott'm Forest. AtleticoTimHortons meet Cowthenbeef next.

matchups.standfirst: Everton's Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall had a hand in both of the Toffees' goals at Hull City, and that carried The Raccoons.
paragraphs: Ainsley Maitland-Niles, signed by domeitalycoach this gameweek, made an assist for his new side in the same 2-2 at Hull.
Cole Palmer, among the most influential men when Chelsea beat Bournemouth 5-1, supplied a pair of assists for The Raccoons.

For domeitalycoach, Man City's Gianluigi Donnarumma kept a clean sheet in a 3-0 win at Liverpool and stood out there. Yeremy, new to their eleven, struck in Crystal Palace's 3-1 win against Nott'm Forest.

matchups.standfirst: Bryan Mbeumo's goal led a Bayern Bru side who found returns right through their eleven.
paragraphs: Mbeumo struck in the 1-1 between Man Utd and Spurs.

Man City's 3-0 win at Liverpool put men from both sides in one match. Marc Guéhi kept a clean sheet there for Bayern Bru, and Rúben matched it for GlengarryHearts. Elliot Anderson, one of the best in that match, set up a goal for GlengarryHearts.
Mohamed Belloumi scored for Hull City against Everton, the only goal GlengarryHearts had.

stories.headline: Henderson, second-hand and first rate
stories.deck: Jordan Henderson's 16 points led a Bin XI that scored 83, more than any side in the league.
stories.body:
Jordan Henderson is the find. Two goals and an assist from midfield in Chelsea's 5-1 dismantling of AFC Bournemouth, with three clearances and an interception for those who like their midfielders honest. Nothing in the bins came near it.

Ipswich Town supply a defence that scores: Dara O'Shea and Abdoul Ouattara each found the net in the 2-1 win over Fulham, with Olivier Boscagli's clean sheet in Brighton & Hove Albion's 2-0 against Sunderland beside them and Konstantinos Tzolakis making four saves in Hull City's 2-2 with Everton. Crystal Palace give the middle its spine, Jefferson Lerma scoring and Quinten Timber providing in the 3-1 over Nottingham Forest, with Jack Rudoni scoring for Coventry City in the 4-1 against Newcastle United. Up front Joe Gelhardt scored and Sorba Thomas provided for Hull, and Jorgen Strand Larsen set one up for Palace.

stories.headline: Lampard's sub plot thickens
stories.deck: Coventry City beat Newcastle United 4-1

reports.standfirst: Coventry City beat Newcastle United 4-1 for their first home win, climbing out of relegation places.
reports.account:
Jack Rudoni put Coventry City ahead from the spot after six minutes, sending his kick low into the corner with his left. Just after half-time Sidiki Cherif doubled the lead, beating the goalkeeper with a low right-foot strike from outside the box.
Sven Botman pulled one back for Newcastle United 20 minutes from time, meeting a pass from Nico González with a shot from distance that flew into the top corner. Ellis Simms, a substitute for Cherif, answered after 81 minutes, turning in Brandon Thomas-Asante's pass from close range. Stephen Mfuni, on for Matt Grimes, made it 4-1 after 86 minutes, turning in a ball from Jay Dasilva inside the box for a second Coventry goal in five minutes. Bazoumana Touré went off injured for Newcastle one minute into stoppage time.

sections.head: Cherif strikes from range
sections.pitch: Sidiki Cherif shot three times for Coventry City, his goal among them, before the substitution that brought on Ellis Simms in his place.
sections.stake: A free agent, nine points; his first league start this season.

sections.head: Rudoni converts
sections.pitch: Jack Rudoni took the kick that opened the scoring, and his conversion was the only goal between the sides at the interval.
sections.stake: A free agent, seven points.

sections.head: Thomas-Asante sets up Simms
sections.pitch: Brandon Thomas-Asante laid on the third goal for Ellis Simms and was also credited with one action in defence for Coventry City.
sections.stake: A free agent, six points.

sections.head: Botman's long-range reply
sections.pitch: Sven Botman's strike was the only goal Newcastle United managed, and it briefly brought them within one before Coventry pulled clear again.
sections.stake: A free agent, six points.

sections.head: González creates six chances
sections.pitch: Nico González set up six openings for Newcastle United, the pass for Sven Botman's goal among them, and he contributed once in defence too.
sections.stake: A free agent, six points.

sections.head: Dasilva tees up Mfuni
sections.pitch: Jay Dasilva supplied the final pass for Stephen Mfuni's goal, the fourth for Coventry City and the last of the match.
sections.stake: A free agent, five points.

sections.head: Simms adds the third
sections.pitch: Ellis Simms took the place of Sidiki Cherif and his goal put two between the sides once more, before Stephen Mfuni added a fourth.
sections.stake: A free agent, five points.

sections.head: van Ewijk
sections.pitch: Milan van Ewijk recorded two defensive actions in a Coventry City defence that gave up a single goal against Newcastle United.
sections.stake: A free agent, six points.

sections.head: Yirenkyi helps the defence
sections.pitch: Caleb Yirenkyi was credited with two contributions without the ball, a figure matched by Milan van Ewijk and Bobby Thomas.
sections.stake: A free agent, four points.

sections.head: Thomas busy in defence
sections.pitch: Bobby Thomas registered a pair of interventions at the back as Coventry City went on to a fourth goal against Newcastle United.
sections.stake: A free agent, four points.

sections.head: Rushworth's four saves
sections.pitch: Carl Rushworth produced four saves for Coventry City, and Newcastle United found a way past him on a single occasion.
sections.stake: A free agent, three points.

stories.headline: Cherki on top
stories.deck: Manchester City won 3-0 at Liverpool

reports.standfirst: Manchester City won 3-0 at Liverpool, scoring all three goals after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off.
reports.account:
Ryan Gravenberch received a second yellow card midway through the second half, leaving Liverpool with ten men at 0-0. Before it, in the 21st minute, Jérémy Jacquet had a shot from close range saved by Gianluigi Donnarumma. Erling Haaland scored three minutes after the red card, left-footed from inside the box and straight down the middle.
Jérémy Doku, on for Iliman Ndiaye, doubled the lead in the 68th minute, turning Elliot Anderson's pass into the top corner with his right foot from inside the area. Rayan Cherki made it 3-0 with 12 minutes left, the third goal in 13 minutes, finishing right-footed from inside the six-yard box after Josko Gvardiol, on for Nico O'Reilly, headed it to him.

sections.head: Doku scores the second
sections.pitch: Jérémy Doku came on from the bench with the match goalless and Liverpool still at full strength, and the goal he scored was the second of City's three.
sections.stake: A free agent since domeitalycoach let him go on Wednesday; eight points.

sections.head: Cherki makes it four
sections.pitch: Rayan Cherki had five shots, and the goal that completed the scoring was his fourth in the league this season.
sections.stake: Cowthenbeef has him, for eight points.

sections.head: Haaland scores, Donnarumma saves
sections.pitch: Erling Haaland's opener took him to six league goals for the season. Gianluigi Donnarumma made six saves and kept a clean sheet behind him.
sections.stake: The Raccoons has Haaland, for six points; domeitalycoach has Donnarumma, for eight points.

reports.standfirst: Crystal Palace came from behind to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1.
reports.account: Daichi Kamada levelled for Crystal Palace just before half-time, taking Quinten Timber's pass and sending a shot low into the corner. Dan Ndoye had put Nottingham Forest in front after three minutes with a low finish from within the area. Jefferson Lerma headed Adam Wharton's corner in from close range in first-half stoppage time, Palace scoring twice in eight minutes. Yéremy Pino struck low from inside the box after 59 minutes for 3-1.

sections.head: Kamada brings Palace level
sections.pitch: Daichi Kamada added a defensive point to the leveller, the goal that began Crystal Palace's recovery from an early deficit.
sections.stake: His eight points are on the bench for The Truffle Pigs, more than the margin by which it trails Cowthenbeef 46-44; Cowthenbeef has one man to play, The Truffle Pigs none.

sections.head: Lerma busy both ends
sections.pitch: Jefferson Lerma tried three shots in all, his headed goal among them, and earned two defensive points at the other end of the pitch.
sections.stake: A free agent, eight points; his first league start this season.

keyStats.label: Points
keyStats.value: Kamada 8 (The Truffle Pigs), Lerma 8, Timber 7, Strand Larsen 6

reports.standfirst: Hull City drew 2-2 with Everton, Mohamed Belloumi levelling from the bench after Thierno Barry's goal.
reports.account:
Thierno Barry put Everton ahead after 68 minutes, striking Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's pass into the top corner. Mohamed Belloumi, on for Joe Gelhardt, levelled with 16 minutes left, his finish from within the area going in high after a pass from Elliot Stroud, a substitute for Ryan Giles.
Barry had a header from close range saved by Konstantinos Tzolakis after 27 minutes, from James Garner's cross. Brennan Johnson's goal for Everton was ruled out after a video review in the 34th minute. Joe Gelhardt opened the scoring just after half-time, meeting Sorba Thomas's through ball on the break and finishing low into the corner. Dewsbury-Hall headed Everton level after 55 minutes from Ainsley Maitland-Niles's corner, the ball going in low.

sections.head: Dewsbury-Hall, Maitland-Niles
sections.pitch: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall had a hand in both Everton goals, taking him to two in the league this season, and created four openings in total with a defensive point besides. Ainsley Maitland-Niles finished with one assist.
sections.stake: The Raccoons has Dewsbury-Hall, for 11 points; domeitalycoach claimed Maitland-Niles on Wednesday, for five points, and trails The Raccoons 47-38; domeitalycoach has two men to play, The Raccoons none.

sections.head: Thomas's assist for Gelhardt
sections.pitch: Sorba Thomas registered one assist and created four chances for Hull City, while also contributing two defensive actions.
sections.stake: A free agent, seven points.

keyStats.label: Points
keyStats.value: Dewsbury-Hall 11 (The Raccoons), Thomas 7, Gelhardt 7, Barry 6 (The Truffle Pigs)

stories.headline: Rice serves Guimarães his winner
stories.deck: Arsenal beat Leeds United 2-1

reports.standfirst: Arsenal came from behind to beat Leeds United 2-1, ending the visitors' unbeaten start.
reports.account: Riccardo Calafiori brought Arsenal level after 62 minutes, meeting Ben White's header with his left foot and sending the ball high into the middle of the goal. James Justin had put Leeds United in front after 55 minutes, turning Gabriel Gudmundsson's cross into the top corner. Bruno Guimarães, on for Myles Lewis-Skelly, won it 20 minutes from time, striking Declan Rice's pass low from outside the box into the corner.

sections.head: Justin's top-corner strike
sections.pitch: James Justin had three shots in the match, and the one from Gabriel Gudmundsson's cross gave Leeds United the only lead they held.
sections.stake: A free agent since Cowthenbeef let him go on Friday; seven points.

sections.head: Guimarães and Rice combine
sections.pitch: Bruno Guimarães now has two league goals this season, this one as a substitute. Declan Rice set it up and earned a defensive point besides.
sections.stake: Guimarães's six points are on the bench for Cowthenbeef; The Truffle Pigs has Rice, for six points.

sections.head: Calafiori, White link up
sections.pitch: Riccardo Calafiori's goal cancelled out Justin's, and it came from Ben White's header, his one assist of the match and the move that set Arsenal on the way back.
sections.stake: AtleticoTimHortons has Calafiori, for eight points; Hazza Maguazza's Redempshazza has White, for five points, and trails AtleticoTimHortons 43-27; Hazza Maguazza's Redempshazza has four men to play, AtleticoTimHortons four.

keyStats.label: Points
keyStats.value: Calafiori 8 (AtleticoTimHortons), Justin 7, Rice 6 (The Truffle Pigs), Guimarães 6 (Cowthenbeef)

reports.standfirst: Brentford remain unbeaten in six after a 2-2 draw at Aston Villa.
reports.account:
John McGinn put Aston Villa 2-1 up with 13 minutes left, sweeping Johan Manzambi's pass into the bottom corner from inside the box. Brentford answered two minutes after McGinn's goal through Kristoffer Ajer, who converted Jaidon Anthony's pass with a low shot.
Yehor Yarmoliuk opened the scoring for the Bees after 10 minutes, his shot going into the middle of the goal. Nicolas Jackson replied for Villa after 12 minutes, finding one corner with a firm drive. Matteo Ruggeri went off injured at the interval. Kevin Schade left the Brentford side injured after 52 minutes.

sections.head: Jackson and Manzambi busy
sections.pitch: Nicolas Jackson took his league total to two with one of his four shots. Johan Manzambi had seven, created three chances, set up McGinn's goal and had chances good enough to score himself.
sections.stake: Jackson's six points are on the bench for The Truffle Pigs, more than the two it trails Cowthenbeef by; Cowthenbeef has Manzambi, for five points.

sections.head: Yarmoliuk's early opener
sections.pitch: Yehor Yarmoliuk's goal was the earliest of the four in this match, and the lead it gave Brentford lasted until Nicolas Jackson's reply.
sections.stake: A free agent, seven points.

keyStats.label: Points
keyStats.value: McGinn 7 (its_ohi), Yarmoliuk 7, Jackson 6 (The Truffle Pigs), Ajer 6

reports.standfirst: Chelsea beat AFC Bournemouth 5-1, leaving the Cherries still without a win this season.
reports.account:
Jordan Henderson struck after two minutes with a low shot from distance into the corner, Cole Palmer supplying the pass. Morgan Rogers sent the ball high into one corner one minute after Henderson's goal, the pass coming from Henderson himself.
João Pedro made it 3-0 just after half-time, sending Pedro Neto's pass up into the corner. Evanilson pulled one back for AFC Bournemouth from a corner after 51 minutes, his close-range effort going high through the middle. A fourth followed midway through the second half, João Pedro meeting Pep Chavarría's cross and finding the top corner. Henderson completed the 5-1 after 70 minutes with a shot into the angle.

sections.head: Henderson in three goals
sections.pitch: Jordan Henderson had three shots, two of which went in, and his pass for Rogers gave him a hand in three of Chelsea's five.
sections.stake: A free agent, 16 points.

sections.head: João Pedro reaches five
sections.pitch: João Pedro's pair takes him to five league goals in the campaign, one from Pedro Neto's pass and the other from Pep Chavarría's cross.
sections.stake: Cowthenbeef has him, for 10 points, and leads The Truffle Pigs 46-44; Cowthenbeef has three men to play, The Truffle Pigs three.

keyStats.label: Points
keyStats.value: Henderson 16, João Pedro 10 (Cowthenbeef), Rogers 9 (If anyone can, Bannan can), Palmer 9 (The Raccoons)

keyStats.label: Chances created
keyStats.value: Henderson 2 (1 assist), Palmer 2 (1 assist), Truffert 2, Gannon-Doak 2

reports.standfirst: Ipswich Town beat Fulham 2-1 with two late goals.
reports.account: Abdoul Ouattara struck for Ipswich Town with two minutes left to make it 1-1, his shot from beyond the area finding the bottom corner. Ryan Sessegnon headed Kenny Tete's cross off target from inside the six-yard box after 24 minutes. He gave Fulham the lead after 55 minutes from a corner, shooting from outside the area. Dara O'Shea completed the turnaround in stoppage time with a low header from close range, substitute Jack Clarke, on for Jaden Philogene, delivering the set-piece cross.

sections.head: Ouattara's long-range leveller
sections.pitch: Abdoul Ouattara's goal ended Fulham's clean sheet with two minutes remaining and brought Ipswich Town back from behind, the winner arriving three minutes later.
sections.stake: A free agent, eight points.

sections.head: O'Shea's set-piece header
sections.pitch: Dara O'Shea's goal was the last of the match and turned a draw into a victory for Ipswich Town against a Fulham side who had led into the closing minutes.
sections.stake: A free agent, eight points.

sections.head: Sessegnon's goal not enough
sections.pitch: Ryan Sessegnon managed three shots, and the one that went in handed Fulham a lead they held for more than half an hour.
sections.stake: A free agent, seven points; his first league start this season.

reports.standfirst: Brighton & Hove Albion beat Sunderland 2-0 despite Pascal Struijk's red card.
reports.account: Pascal Struijk was sent off after 57 minutes with Brighton & Hove Albion a goal up, yet his side still added a second. Thomas Meunier had gone off injured for Sunderland after 34 minutes. Maxim De Cuyper put Brighton in front after 53 minutes, converting Pascal Groß's pass. Jaouen Hadjam, on for Diego Gómez, doubled the lead in stoppage time on the break from a through ball by fellow substitute Georginio Rutter, on for Yasin Ayari.

sections.head: Hadjam's late second
sections.pitch: Jaouen Hadjam had been on the pitch for a matter of minutes when his goal arrived, the second for a Brighton side playing with ten men.
sections.stake: A free agent, seven points.

sections.head: De Cuyper
sections.pitch: Maxim De Cuyper's goal was his second of the league season, set up by Pascal Groß, and he earned a defensive point alongside it.
sections.stake: AtleticoTimHortons has him, for nine points.

keyStats.label: Points
keyStats.value: De Cuyper 9 (AtleticoTimHortons), Verbruggen 7 (Cowthenbeef), Vuskovic 7 (The Truffle Pigs), Kadioglu 7 (The Truffle Pigs)

reports.standfirst: Ten-man Tottenham Hotspur drew 1-1 with Manchester United through a late equaliser.
reports.account: Rodrigo Bentancur's dismissal five minutes after Bryan Mbeumo's goal left Tottenham Hotspur a man down and a goal behind. Mbeumo had put Manchester United ahead after 73 minutes, taking Matheus Cunha's pass inside the box and steering a finish from his sinister foot down into the corner. Dominic Solanke levelled two minutes into stoppage time, meeting Sandro Tonali's cross inside the box and heading down into the corner.

sections.head: Solanke's late header
sections.pitch: Dominic Solanke had four shots in the match, and his equaliser was the only one of them that went in.
sections.stake: A free agent, six points.

sections.head: Cunha's assist
sections.pitch: Matheus Cunha's pass made the only goal Manchester United scored, an opener that kept them ahead of Tottenham until stoppage time.
sections.stake: its_ohi has him, for seven points, and leads If anyone can, Bannan can 40-34; its_ohi has four men to play, If anyone can, Bannan can three.

stories.headline: Lawro's Power Rankings
stories.deck: Lawro ranks the ten drafted squads, with GlengarryHearts the strongest and Hazza Maguazza's Redempshazza the weakest.
stories.body: Twenty-two years predicting scores on the BBC. Now I rank fantasy squads for a paper named after doughnuts. Nobody is clear, but GlengarryHearts have the toughest defenders and Hazza Maguazza's Redempshazza a midfield that wants a lie down.

ranks.line: Isak was the first man drafted here, and the forwards around him couldn't trap a bag of cement. Strongest squad going, and I'm still not happy.
Forwards? Thin. It all rests on Morgan Rogers, and the lad's only got two legs.
Haaland at one end, and at the other a goalkeeper who couldn't catch a cold. Lovely balance, that.
Softest defenders in the league, and I've had firmer custard. Bruno Fernandes was the first name in the whole draft, and he doesn't defend.
Semenyo, a City man, is the cornerstone. The rest of the forwards wouldn't get a game in my local pub side.
A midfield this flimsy would blow over in a stiff breeze. João Pedro went first for them, and there's precious little beef behind him.
Kostoulas of Brighton was their opening choice, well down the menu. I've seen more going on in a bus queue than this midfield.
No goalkeeper in the league is worse, and I've seen better ones in the park on a Sunday. They started with Ødegaard, and passing never stopped a shot yet.
Wirtz is the man they built round, and a tidy one, which annoys me. The defenders would wave a milk float through.
This midfield is a shambles and nobody need pretend otherwise. Saka was taken early, and one lad can't hold a whole house up.
